standard_text: Addition and subtraction of 2- and 3-digit numbers using mental strategies, the link between addition and subtraction, and daily-life problems (summary of NCERT Maths Mela Class 3)
meta_desc: Class 3 Vacation with My Nani Maa worksheet (Maths Mela Chapter 4): mental strategies, fact families, missing numbers and word problems. 100 questions with answers.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Add tens first, then ones: 45 + 38 = 75 + 8 = 83.
  • Use a near ten: 57 + 19 = 57 + 20 − 1 = 76.
  • Check a subtraction by adding back.

Examples

Example

64 + 29

64 + 30 = 94

94 − 1

Answer: 93

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Forgetting to take back the 1 after adding 20 for 19Adding 20 adds 1 too many.
Subtracting the smaller digit from the bigger in each placeBreak a ten when the top digit is smaller.

faq.a: Facts with the same three numbers: 8 + 5 = 13, 5 + 8 = 13, 13 − 5 = 8, 13 − 8 = 5.
They make many sums quick without writing.

items.q: 15 − 7 = 8. Use this fact. What is 150 − 70?
items.e: 150 is 15 tens and 70 is 7 tens. 15 tens − 7 tens = 8 tens = 80.

items.q: 12 − 5 = 7. Use this fact. What is 120 − 50?
items.e: 120 is 12 tens and 50 is 5 tens. 12 tens − 5 tens = 7 tens = 70.

items.q: 13 − 4 = 9. Use this fact. What is 130 − 40?
items.e: 130 is 13 tens and 40 is 4 tens. 13 tens − 4 tens = 9 tens = 90.

items.q: Which fact helps you work out 80 + 60?
items.e: 80 is 8 tens and 60 is 6 tens. Use 8 + 6 = 14: 14 tens = 140.

items.q: Which fact helps you work out 140 − 90?
items.e: 140 is 14 tens and 90 is 9 tens. Use 14 − 9 = 5: 5 tens = 50.

items.q: 7 + 8 = 15. Use this fact. What is 47 + 8?
items.e: 7 + 8 = 15, which is 1 ten and 5 ones. So the tens go up by 1: 47 + 8 = 55.

items.q: What is 36 + 9?
items.e: 6 + 9 = 15, which is 1 ten and 5 ones. So the tens go up by 1: 36 + 9 = 45.

items.q: 8 + 5 = 13. Use this fact. What is 68 + 5?
items.e: 8 + 5 = 13, which is 1 ten and 3 ones. So the tens go up by 1: 68 + 5 = 73.

items.q: What is 256 + 7?
items.e: 6 + 7 = 13, which is 1 ten and 3 ones. So the tens go up by 1: 256 + 7 = 263.

items.q: What is 485 + 9?
items.e: 5 + 9 = 14, which is 1 ten and 4 ones. So the tens go up by 1: 485 + 9 = 494.

items.q: 13 − 5 = 8. Use this fact. What is 63 − 5?
items.e: You cannot take 5 from 3 ones. Use 13 − 5 = 8. The tens go down by 1: 63 − 5 = 58.

items.q: What is 42 − 7?
items.e: You cannot take 7 from 2 ones. Use 12 − 7 = 5. The tens go down by 1: 42 − 7 = 35.

items.q: 11 − 6 = 5. Use this fact. What is 81 − 6?
items.e: You cannot take 6 from 1 one. Use 11 − 6 = 5. The tens go down by 1: 81 − 6 = 75.

items.q: What is 234 − 8?
items.e: You cannot take 8 from 4 ones. Use 14 − 8 = 6. The tens go down by 1: 234 − 8 = 226.

items.q: Add. Regroup when a column makes 10 or more.
items.e: Line up the ones and start on the right. Ones: 6 + 2 = 8. Tens: 6 + 1 = 7. Hundreds: 4 + 4 = 8. Answer: 878.

items.q: Add. Regroup when a column makes 10 or more.
items.e: Line up the ones and start on the right. Ones: 2 + 3 = 5. Tens: 5 + 4 = 9. Hundreds: 4 + 1 = 5. Answer: 595.

items.q: Use the column method. What is 139 + 787?
items.e: Line up the ones and start on the right. Ones: 9 + 7 = 16. Write 6 and regroup 10 ones as 1 ten. Tens: 3 + 8 + 1 = 12. Write 2 and regroup 10 tens as 1 hundred. Hundreds: 1 + 7 + 1 = 9. Answer: 926.

items.q: Add. Regroup when a column makes 10 or more.
items.e: Line up the ones and start on the right. Ones: 8 + 4 = 12. Write 2 and regroup 10 ones as 1 ten. Tens: 7 + 6 + 1 = 14. Write 4 and regroup 10 tens as 1 hundred. Hundreds: 4 + 1 + 1 = 6. Answer: 642.

items.q: Use the column method. What is 673 + 58?
items.e: Line up the ones and start on the right. Ones: 3 + 8 = 11. Write 1 and regroup 10 ones as 1 ten. Tens: 7 + 5 + 1 = 13. Write 3 and regroup 10 tens as 1 hundred. Hundreds: 6 + 1 = 7. Answer: 731.

items.q: Add. Regroup when a column makes 10 or more.
items.e: Line up the ones and start on the right. Ones: 9 + 7 = 16. Write 6 and regroup 10 ones as 1 ten. Tens: 7 + 3 + 1 = 11. Write 1 and regroup 10 tens as 1 hundred. Hundreds: 7 + 1 = 8. Answer: 816.

items.q: Jump to 60 first. What is 58 + 7?
Jump to 90 first. What is 86 + 6?
Jump back to 50 first. What is 53 − 8?
To work out 38 + 7, you jump to 40 first. How do you split the 7?
items.e: 38 needs 2 to make 40. Then 5 more: 40 + 5 = 45. So split 7 into 2 and 5.

items.q: To work out 64 − 9, you jump back to 60 first. How do you split the 9?
items.e: 64 − 4 = 60. Then 5 more: 60 − 5 = 55. So split 9 into 4 and 5.

items.q: Jump the tens, then the ones. What is 45 + 32?
items.e: 45 + 30 = 75. Then 75 + 2 = 77. (75 stops after the tens.)

items.q: Jump back the tens, then the ones. What is 86 − 43?
items.e: 86 − 40 = 46. Then 46 − 3 = 43. (46 stops after the tens.)

items.q: Jump the tens, then the ones. What is 158 + 25?
Jump back the tens, then the ones. What is 124 − 36?
Use double 25. What is 25 + 26?
items.e: Double 25 is 50. 26 is 1 more than 25, so add 1: 50 + 1 = 51.

items.q: What is 436 + 200?
items.e: Only the hundreds change. 4 hundreds + 2 hundreds = 6 hundreds. 436 + 200 = 636.

items.q: What is 758 − 40?
items.e: Only the tens change. 5 tens − 4 tens = 1 ten. 758 − 40 = 718.

items.q: Use the split strategy. What is 324 + 152?
Use the split strategy. What is 258 + 126?
items.e: Split both numbers: 200 + 50 + 8 and 100 + 20 + 6. Hundreds: 200 + 100 = 300. Tens: 50 + 20 = 70. Ones: 8 + 6 = 14. 14 ones is 1 ten and 4 ones. 300 + 70 + 14 = 384.

items.q: Use the split strategy. What is 368 + 427?
items.e: Split both numbers: 300 + 60 + 8 and 400 + 20 + 7. Hundreds: 300 + 400 = 700. Tens: 60 + 20 = 80. Ones: 8 + 7 = 15. 15 ones is 1 ten and 5 ones. 700 + 80 + 15 = 795.

items.q: Use the split strategy. 356 + 128 = 400 + ? + 14
items.e: Tens: 50 + 20 = 70. Hundreds: 300 + 100 = 400. Ones: 6 + 8 = 14. 400 + 70 + 14 = 484. (80 would count the regrouped ten twice: the 14 already holds it.)
Count each kind of block. Hundreds: 2 + 1 = 3. Tens: 4 + 3 = 7. Ones: 6 + 7 = 13. Regroup 10 ones as 1 ten: 8 tens and 3 ones. The total is 383.

items.q: Start at 368. Jump forward 200, then 20, then 5. Where do you land?
Start at 815. Jump back 300, then 60, then 7. Where do you land?
Where does the last jump land?
Which addition matches the model?
items.e: Add the two parts to make the whole: 36 + 47 = 83.

items.q: Which subtraction matches the model?
items.e: Start with the whole and take away one part. The other part is left: 150 − 90 = 60.

items.q: Addition and subtraction are inverse operations. What does this mean?
items.e: Inverse means opposite. If you add 30 and then take away 30, you are back where you started. They undo each other.

items.q: How many facts are in the fact family for 30, 50 and 80?
28 + 55 = 83. Which is also true?
items.e: Subtraction undoes addition. Start with the whole, 83, and take away 55: 83 − 55 = 28.

items.q: 120 − 70 = 50. Which is also true?
items.e: Addition undoes subtraction. Add the two parts to get back to 120: 50 + 70 = 120.

items.q: Start with 64. Add 29. Then take away 29. What number do you get?
items.e: Taking away 29 undoes adding 29. You get back to the start: 64.

items.q: You know 46 + 37 = 83. What is 83 − 46?
items.e: 46 and 37 are the parts and 83 is the whole. Whole − one part = the other part: 37.

items.q: What is the missing part?
items.e: Whole − part = the other part. 120 − 45: 120 − 40 = 80, then 80 − 5 = 75. Check: 45 + 75 = 120.

items.q: What is the missing part?
items.e: Count on from 130 to 200: 130 + 70 = 200. The missing part is 70.

items.q: Which addition checks 523 − 168 = 355?
items.e: To check a subtraction, add the answer and the number you took away. You should get the number you started with: 355 + 168 = 523.

items.q: Which subtraction checks 384 + 279 = 663?
items.e: To check an addition, start with the total and take away one of the numbers. You should get the other number: 663 − 279 = 384.

items.q: Which fact is in the same fact family as 245 + 318 = 563?
items.e: A fact family uses the same three numbers: 245, 318 and 563. The total minus one part gives the other part: 563 − 245 = 318. (563 − 318 is 245, not 254.)

items.q: Gauri adds 368 + 457 and gets 825. Which subtraction checks her answer?
items.e: Start with the total and take away 457. You should get the first number: 825 − 457 = 368. It works, so 825 is right.

items.q: Priya says 543 − 278 = 265. Check with addition. What is 265 + 278?
items.e: Add the answer and the number taken away: 265 + 278 = 543. That is the number she started with, so her answer is right.

items.q: Aarav says 702 − 356 = 454. Check with addition. What is 454 + 356?
items.e: Add the answer and the number taken away: 454 + 356 = 810. That is not 702, so his answer is wrong. The correct answer is 702 − 356 = 346.

items.q: Tara says 600 − 245 = 365. Check with addition. What is 365 + 245?
items.e: Add the answer and the number taken away: 365 + 245 = 610. That is not 600, so her answer is wrong. The correct answer is 600 − 245 = 355.

items.q: Rahul says 914 − 387 = 527. Check with addition. What is 527 + 387?
items.e: Add the answer and the number taken away: 527 + 387 = 914. That is the number he started with, so his answer is right.

items.q: Kavya says 821 − 465 = 466. Check with addition. What is 466 + 465?
items.e: Add the answer and the number taken away: 466 + 465 = 931. That is not 821, so her answer is wrong. The correct answer is 821 − 465 = 356.

items.q: Dev says 734 − 46 = 274. Check with addition. What is 274 + 46?
items.e: Add the answer and the number taken away: 274 + 46 = 320. That is not 734, so his answer is wrong. The correct answer is 734 − 46 = 688.

items.q: Find the missing number: ? + 45 = 120
items.e: Use the inverse: 120 − 45. 120 − 40 = 80, then 80 − 5 = 75. Check: 75 + 45 = 120. (120 is the total, not the missing part.)

items.q: Find the missing number: 57 + ? = 100
Find the missing number: 68 = ? + 30
items.e: The = sign means both sides are the same. ? + 30 = 68, so 68 − 30 = 38. Check: 38 + 30 = 68.

items.q: Find the missing number: ? + 26 = 81
Find the missing number: 90 − ? = 35
Find the missing number: ? − 40 = 85
items.e: Use the inverse: 85 + 40 = 125. Check: 125 − 40 = 85. (45 takes away instead of adding.)

items.q: Find the missing number: ? − 25 = 48
Find the missing number: 140 = 90 + ?
Find the missing number: 200 − ? = 120
items.e: Count on from 120 to 200: 8 tens = 80. Check: 200 − 80 = 120.

items.q: Find the missing number: 300 − ? = 175
Find the missing number: 500 − ? = 350
Find the missing number: ? + 175 = 300
items.e: Use the inverse: 300 − 175. Count on 25 to 200 and 100 to 300: 125. Check: 125 + 175 = 300.

items.q: Find the missing number: ? − 130 = 270
Find the missing number: 650 = ? + 280
Find the missing number: 40 + 25 = ? + 30
items.e: Both sides must have the same value. 40 + 25 = 65, so ? + 30 = 65 and ? = 35. (65 is only the left side.)

items.q: Find the missing number: 70 + 50 = 60 + ?
Find the missing number: 100 − 30 = ? − 40
Find the missing number: 38 + 9 = ? + 10
items.e: 10 is 1 more than 9, so the other number must be 1 less than 38: 37. Check: 38 + 9 = 47 and 37 + 10 = 47.

items.q: Find the missing number: 64 − 19 = ? − 20
Which number sentence is true?
items.e: 45 + 15 = 60 and 70 − 10 = 60. Both sides are the same, so 45 + 15 = 70 − 10 is true.

items.q: Diya has 45 stickers. She gets some more. Now she has 120 stickers. Which number sentence shows this?
items.e: Start with 45, add an unknown amount, and end with 120: 45 + ? = 120. The missing number is 75.

items.q: The canteen had 300 icy poles. Some were sold. Now 175 are left. Which number sentence shows this?
items.e: Start with 300, take away an unknown amount, and 175 are left: 300 − ? = 175. The missing number is 125.

items.q: Some students are on a bus. 30 more get on. Now there are 68 students on the bus. Which number sentence shows this?
items.e: We do not know the start. Add 30 to get 68: ? + 30 = 68. The missing number is 38.

items.q: Manav reads 47 pages on Monday and 38 pages on Tuesday. How many pages is that altogether? Which number sentence shows this?
items.e: Altogether means add the two amounts: 47 + 38 = ?. The answer is 85.

items.q: There are 92 people at the pool. 58 go home. How many are still at the pool? Which number sentence shows this?
items.e: Start with 92 and take away 58: 92 − 58 = ?. Put the bigger number first. The answer is 34.

items.q: Shreya had some marbles. She gave away 40. Now she has 85 left. Which number sentence shows this?
items.e: We do not know the start. Take away 40 and 85 are left: ? − 40 = 85. The missing number is 125.

items.q: The hall needs 100 chairs for assembly. 57 chairs are set out. How many more are needed? Which number sentence shows this?
items.e: 57 and some more make 100: 57 + ? = 100. The missing number is 43.

items.q: At the swimming carnival, 160 students are at the pool. 70 of them are in the water. How many are not in the water?
items.e: Take away the 70 in the water. 16 tens − 7 tens = 9 tens, so 90 students.

items.q: Yash scores 39 points in a game. Then he scores 26 more. How many points does he have now?
items.e: Add. 39 is 1 less than 40. 40 + 26 = 66, then take away 1: 65 points.

items.q: Class 3 Blue has 25 students. Class 3 Gold has 26 students. How many students are there in the two classes?
items.e: Use a near double. Double 25 is 50, and 1 more is 51 students.

items.q: The Class 3 bake sale sold 168 muffins and 254 biscuits. How many treats did it sell altogether?
items.e: Altogether means add. 168 + 254 = 422. Check: 422 − 254 = 168.

items.q: On the way to the cottage, the Chen family drove 186 km before lunch and 147 km after lunch. How far did they drive?
items.e: Put the two parts of the trip together, so add. 186 + 147 = 333. Check: 333 − 147 = 186.

items.q: Kavya read 245 pages in October and 178 pages in November. How many pages did she read in the two months?
items.e: Put the two months together, so add. 245 + 178 = 423. Check: 423 − 178 = 245.

items.q: Dev’s book has 312 pages. He has read 148 pages. How many pages are left?
items.e: Find what is left, so subtract. 312 − 148 = 164. Check: 164 + 148 = 312.

items.q: The cottage is 403 km from home. The family has driven 165 km. How many kilometres are left?
items.e: Find the distance left, so subtract. 403 − 165 = 238. Check: 238 + 165 = 403.

items.q: The school bought 600 freezies for the fun fair. 437 freezies were sold. How many freezies were left?
items.e: Sold ones are taken away, so subtract. 600 − 437 = 163. Check: 163 + 437 = 600.

items.q: At the hockey arena, 924 people watched the game on Saturday and 657 people watched on Sunday. How many more people came on Saturday?
items.e: How many more means find the difference, so subtract. 924 − 657 = 267. Check: 267 + 657 = 924.

items.q: Nisha had some hockey cards. She got 145 more for her birthday. Now she has 403 cards. How many cards did she have at the start?
items.e: Work backwards. Take away the 145 that were added: 403 − 145 = 258. Check: 258 + 145 = 403.

items.q: The charity box had some cans. 175 cans were taken to charity. Now 389 cans are left. How many cans were in the box at the start?
items.e: Work backwards. Add back the 175 that were taken away: 389 + 175 = 564. Check: 564 − 175 = 389.

items.q: Aditi’s book has 400 pages. She read 132 pages on the weekend and 89 pages on Monday. How many pages are left to read?
items.e: Step 1, pages read: 132 + 89 = 221. Step 2, pages left: 400 − 221 = 179.
